entities.name: Tommaso Orsini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tommaso Orsini (b. 1350, Rome – d. July 18, 1390, Narni) was a prominent Italian cardinal and prelate, a scion of the influential Roman Orsini family, whose career was intrinsically linked to the tumultuous political and religious landscape of 14th-century Italy, particularly the Great Western Schism. Rising through the ecclesiastical ranks during a period of intense papal rivalries and the return of the papacy to Rome, Orsini’s life exemplifies the convergence of noble power, church politics, and the burgeoning mercantile interests within the Papal States. His actions and affiliations significantly impacted the stability of the Roman Curia and the broader efforts to heal the schism, making him a figure of considerable regional, if not continental, importance.

Elevated to the cardinalate by Pope Urban VI in 1385, Tommaso Orsini had previously served as Bishop of Narni from 1378, a strategic see in Umbria. His appointment as cardinal-deacon of Santa Maria in Domnica cemented his position within the College of Cardinals during a period when Urban VI was striving to consolidate his authority against the Avignon antipopes Clement VII and Benedict XIII. Orsini, leveraging his family's extensive networks and considerable wealth, was instrumental in securing support for the Roman obedience, participating in various consistories and diplomatic missions aimed at bolstering Urban VI's legitimacy and influence throughout central Italy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Tommaso Orsini's cardinalate provided critical support to Pope Urban VI during the volatile early years of the Great Western Schism, helping to stabilize the Roman obedience. His actions, backed by the powerful Orsini family, reinforced the Papal States' political structure amidst profound ecclesiastical division.
